text: 25 m across, the silo encloses a 17 m bore.
Ten jumpform lifts take the shell to 32 m. The circular raft is 2 m thick.
Duplex stainless hoop bars carry tension in the outer wall. A bonded liner accommodates the design crack opening of roughly 0.4 mm.
The tandem lift uses 62 m booms. Liebherr’s LR 1300 is a 300 t class reference. Capacity depends on radius.
Four radial arms restrain the shaft laterally. The collar allows vertical movement.
Each four-rack pod spans 7.16 m. The receiving lane handles two pods per delivery.
Eight levels accommodate 64 pods and 256 racks.
Thirty dry coolers provide 60 MW of nominal heat rejection.
Bulk propane supplies both gas turbines. Diesel has a separate storage and transfer system, reserved for declared emergencies.
The annulus holds over 6,500 m³ of glycol solution.
Each turbine package has an assumed mass of 94.5 t, carried on independent rail girders.
Four diesels cover 7 MW of priority computing. Cat’s 3516C is a standby reference.
The design assumes two 25 MW propane turbines. For comparison, GE’s LM2500 DLE delivers 22.7 MW net on natural gas at ISO conditions.
Three operator consoles share the building with the receiving lane.
The shaft stays fixed. Its 50.8 mm wall supports a carrier indexing in 45° steps.
Four Vera Rubin racks, 72 GPUs apiece, have a combined design allowance of 780 kW.
The coolers are rated at 2 MW each. Güntner’s V-shape VARIO reaches that capacity class.
The exhaust basis per turbine is 70 kg/s at 566 °C.
Four megawatts of auxiliaries leave 46 MW for computing. One dispatch runs 235 racks at full power with 21 spare. Operators can distribute that load across more racks.
With circulation available, a 10 K swing in the stratified store gives 76 minutes of modelled cooling ride-through at full design heat load.
